name: Sentinel-2 geo-foundation model encoders used frozen

identity.method_name: Frozen Sentinel-2 / Earth-observation foundation-model encoders (SSL4EO-S12, Prithvi-EO-2.0, TerraMind v1.0, Clay v1.5, SatMAE) used as fixed feature extractors feeding a small trainable head; RS-MTDF-style frozen-teacher (DINOv2, CLIP) knowledge distillation into a small student as the lighter alternative
identity.core_idea: Instead of training a CNN/transformer from scratch on the project's 42 lake-year scenes, run each patch through a much larger network that was pretrained with a self-supervised objective (masked-autoencoding, contrastive/DINO, or generative token-masking) on millions of unlabelled global Sentinel-2/HLS chips, keep every weight in that network frozen, and train only a small linear or shallow head on top of the resulting embedding. The knowledge-distillation alternative is lighter at deployment time: a frozen large teacher (DINOv2 and/or CLIP, as in RS-MTDF) produces target features once, and a small student network is trained to match them plus the task loss, so only the small student needs to be shipped or re-run, though building the distillation loop is not necessarily less implementation effort than plain frozen-feature probing.
identity.official_dataset_ids: SSL4EO-S12 dataset/weights: zhu-xlab/SSL4EO-S12 (GitHub), mediaTUM DOI 10.14459/2022mp1656045; TorchGeo weight IDs torchgeo/resnet18_sentinel2_all_moco, torchgeo/resnet50_sentinel2_all_dino, torchgeo/vit_small_patch16_224_sentinel2_all_moco. Prithvi-EO-2.0: ibm-nasa-geospatial/Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M, ibm-nasa-geospatial/Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL, ibm-nasa-geospatial/Prithvi-EO-2.0-600M, ibm-nasa-geospatial/Prithvi-EO-2.0-600M-TL (Hugging Face). TerraMind v1.0: ibm-esa-geospatial/TerraMind-1.0-tiny, -small, -base, -large (Hugging Face), pretrained on the TerraMesh dataset. Clay v1.5: made-with-clay/Clay, checkpoint v1.5/clay-v1.5.ckpt (Hugging Face). SatMAE: sustainlab-group/SatMAE (GitHub code); pretrained on fMoW-Sentinel (no formal catalog dataset ID). RS-MTDF distillation code: earth-insights/RS-MTDF (GitHub); teachers facebookresearch/dinov2 and openai/CLIP (or mlfoundations/open_clip).

fit_to_project.ground_truth_proxy_strategy: None of these five encoders supplies an encroachment label by themselves; 'frozen feature extraction' only changes the feature space fed to a downstream head, and that head still needs a training signal. Three honest options, in increasing cost: (a) fully unsupervised -- cluster the 42 (or per-tile) embeddings and flag lakes/years that are outliers relative to their own history, with zero labelling cost but no guarantee the outlier axis is 'encroachment' rather than desilting, cloud contamination, or sensor drift; (b) programmatic weak supervision -- reuse the project's own MNDWI>0 / NDVI>0.30 rule as a pseudo-label to train a linear probe on the embeddings, at effectively zero extra annotation cost, but this only teaches the probe to reproduce the existing baseline's biases (including both stated confounds) in a new feature space; (c) a small amount of manual annotation -- the student hand-flags perhaps 10-15 lake-years as 'visually consistent with encroachment' vs 'not' from the true-colour composite plus outside knowledge (news reports, KTCDA records), then trains the linear probe on that, at an estimated 2-4 student-days, still not real ground truth and highly subjective. None of these three is 'zero-shot foundation model' in the sense of a class-name text prompt (only CLIP, inside the distillation route, supports that, and CLIP was never trained on satellite imagery).
fit_to_project.input_required: A 20 m multiband raster patch per lake-year with band identity, order and (for some models) grid resolution matching what each encoder expects at pretraining time. The project already has the raw patches (B02, B03, B04, B08, B11, SCL at 20 m EPSG:32643); whether that satisfies a given encoder's input contract without re-downloading extra bands or reprojecting is model-specific -- see resolution_match_20m and licence for the per-model breakdown that follows.
fit_to_project.viable_with_42_rows: only-if-reframed. All five encoders operate on a fixed-size image patch/token grid, not on a 42-row tabular record. If the student runs exactly one forward pass per lake-year (one patch covering each lake's OpenStreetMap footprint), the effective sample count for any downstream linear probe stays at 42 (same as the current tabular pipeline), just with a richer feature vector per row instead of hand-engineered MNDWI/NDVI statistics. If instead the patch is tiled into the encoder's native tokens (e.g. 16x16 px tokens for a ViT with patch size 16), a single lake-year decomposes into tens to a few hundred token embeddings, but those tokens are not independent samples for validation purposes (they share the same shoreline, same sensor look, same year) and would still require a pixel/token-level proxy label (see ground_truth_proxy_strategy) to be usable as anything other than a pooled feature for the 42-row case.
fit_to_project.viable_without_ground_truth: needs-weak-labels. See ground_truth_proxy_strategy for the exact source and cost of the weak signal; none of the five encoders removes this requirement.
fit_to_project.resolution_match_20m: Model-by-model, since this varies sharply: SSL4EO-S12 was pretrained on native Sentinel-2 10/20/60 m bands packed to a common 10 m grid -- broadly compatible with the project's 20 m grid, no severe mismatch. Prithvi-EO-2.0 was pretrained exclusively on NASA HLS at 30 m -- this IS the flagged case: applying weights trained at 30 m Landsat-harmonised resolution to the project's native 20 m Sentinel-2 grid without resampling is a genuine resolution mismatch, not merely a band-naming one. TerraMind v1.0 was pretrained on native-resolution Sentinel-2 L2A bands (10 m/20 m mixed) via the TerraMesh dataset -- reasonably matched. Clay v1.5 explicitly conditions on ground-sample-distance (GSD) as an input signal and was pretrained across many sensors/resolutions (10 m-60 m and sub-metre aerial mixed) -- GSD-aware design makes 20 m usage plausible, though most Clay S2 pretraining chips were 10 m. SatMAE was pretrained on fMoW-Sentinel at native S2 10/20/60 m -- matched for the shared bands. RS-MTDF's two teachers, DINOv2 and CLIP, were pretrained entirely on natural RGB photographs (ImageNet-scale web images) with no satellite provenance at all -- this is the clearest instance in this whole item of a model pretrained on sub-metre/arbitrary-scale imagery being applied to 20 m reflectance data, and it is a real domain gap, not just a resolution number mismatch.
fit_to_project.label_source_needed: None for the frozen encoders themselves (self-supervised pretraining, no labels involved at all); the downstream head needs weak labels as described in ground_truth_proxy_strategy (MNDWI/NDVI rule output, or a small manually flagged subset).
fit_to_project.fixes_which_stated_limitation: Does not fix (1) 42 rows: adopting a bigger encoder changes feature quality per row, not row count, unless the student explicitly reframes to pixel/token level with a proxy label (see viable_with_42_rows), which reintroduces limitation (3) at pixel scale. Does not fix (2), the static single-snapshot OpenStreetMap building problem; that is an entirely separate data source these encoders do not touch. Does not fix (3), no real ground truth: every one of these encoders still needs a label or proxy for its downstream head, and self-supervised pretraining supplies representation quality, not supervision. Could partially help (4), one dry-season scene per year, only for the models with an explicit multi-temporal input path (SatMAE's temporal encoding, Prithvi's spatiotemporal 3-D embeddings, TerraMind's temporal conditioning) -- but only if the student separately acquires additional intra-year scenes to feed them; with the current one-scene-per-year cache, these models all run in degraded single-timestep mode and gain nothing over a simpler single-frame encoder.
fit_to_project.handles_desilting_confound: No. A frozen encoder's embedding still summarises what the reflectance and texture in the patch look like; it has no built-in notion of *why* water disappeared. A 20 m, 5-6 band patch of a lake drained for desilting (exposed wet mud/silt, later returning to water) and a patch of the same lake genuinely filled by construction can present visually similar 'less water, more bare/vegetated surface' signatures at this resolution and band set, and none of the five encoders were pretrained with any label distinguishing hydrological drawdown from permanent land conversion. Separating them would require an explicit multi-temporal trajectory feature built on top of the embeddings (does the patch return to full water within 1-2 years, or not) plus external corroboration (KTCDA desilting project records, since OpenStreetMap buildings are static and cannot help here) -- additional engineering the encoder does not supply for free.
fit_to_project.handles_hyacinth_confound: Partially and speculatively, better than the current NDVI>0.30 rule in principle, but unverified for this exact problem. Self-supervised MAE/DINO objectives learn broader texture and context than a single spectral index, so an embedding might separate the mottled, patchy texture of a hyacinth mat from the more uniform texture of shoreline vegetation or built-up land better than a hard NDVI threshold -- but none of SSL4EO-S12, Prithvi-EO-2.0, TerraMind, Clay, or SatMAE were pretrained or benchmarked on aquatic macrophyte classes specifically, so this benefit is a hypothesis, not a documented result. It must be checked directly against Bareuther, Klinge & Buerkert (2020), MDPI Remote Sensing 12(22):3843, doi 10.3390/rs12223843, which independently mapped macrophyte cover for Bellandur and Varthur, before any claim of improvement over the baseline on this specific confound is made.
fit_to_project.legal_traceability: None of the five encoders changes this at all. They produce feature embeddings from imagery inside whatever polygon is supplied (currently the OpenStreetMap multipolygon); none references the Bengaluru Master Plan 30 m buffer, the earlier NGT 75 m buffer, Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority records, Survey of India records, Bhuvan, or the National Wetland Atlas 2024. Legal traceability for this item is exactly as good, or as absent, as the project's existing baseline -- the choice of encoder does not touch this field.
fit_to_project.temporal_granularity: The five encoders are stateless per input scene, and every one of the project's 6 cached spectral bands (B02, B03, B04, B08, B11) plus SCL already varies year to year (one real L2A scene per lake-year), so adopting a frozen encoder introduces no NEW static-snapshot problem of the kind the OpenStreetMap building counts have. The caveat is architectural under-use: SatMAE's temporal positional encoding, Prithvi's 3-D spatiotemporal embedding, and TerraMind's temporal conditioning are all designed for multiple images per location per year; fed only the project's single dry-season scene, they degrade to an ordinary single-frame encoder and their main architectural selling point over SSL4EO-S12/Clay is unused.

implementation.libraries: SSL4EO-S12 / SatMAE: PyTorch, timm, torchgeo>=0.5 (for pre-wrapped SSL4EO-S12 weight enums). Prithvi-EO-2.0 / TerraMind: terratorch (IBM TerraTorch), transformers, huggingface_hub, rasterio, einops. Clay v1.5: the claymodel Python package (or a direct PyTorch Lightning checkpoint load), stackstac, einops. RS-MTDF distillation: PyTorch, facebookresearch/dinov2, openai/CLIP or mlfoundations/open_clip, plus a standard segmentation training loop (e.g. a small U-Net-style student decoder).
implementation.pretrained_weights: SSL4EO-S12: ResNet18/50 and ViT-Small backbones, pretrained on 13-band Sentinel-2 L1C (top-of-atmosphere) at up to 10 m resampled grid, hosted on Hugging Face under the torchgeo org and mediaTUM. Prithvi-EO-2.0: ViT-Base/Large (300M/600M parameter) masked-autoencoder backbones, pretrained on NASA HLS V2 (Landsat+Sentinel-2 harmonised) at 30 m, hosted at huggingface.co/ibm-nasa-geospatial. TerraMind v1.0: dual-scale transformer encoder-decoder, tiny/small/base/large, pretrained on the 9-modality, 9M-sample TerraMesh dataset (mixed native S2 L2A resolutions), hosted at huggingface.co/ibm-esa-geospatial. Clay v1.5: ViT-based masked-autoencoder with a wavelength- and GSD-aware dynamic patch embedding, pretrained on ~70M chips across many sensors and resolutions (Sept 2024 run, 20x AWS g6.48xlarge instances), hosted at huggingface.co/made-with-clay/Clay (checkpoint ~5.16 GB). SatMAE: ViT-Large masked-autoencoder, pretrained on fMoW-Sentinel at native S2 10/20/60 m grouped bands, hosted on the sustainlab-group GitHub release assets. DINOv2 (ViT-S/B/L/g) and CLIP (ViT-B/16, ViT-L/14, etc.) are pretrained on natural RGB web images (LVD-142M and WIT respectively), hosted on facebookresearch/dinov2 and openai/CLIP / Hugging Face.
implementation.licence: SSL4EO-S12: code Apache-2.0, dataset and pretrained weights CC-BY-4.0 -- usable academically with attribution. Prithvi-EO-2.0: Apache-2.0 (code and weights) -- fully permissive. TerraMind v1.0: Apache-2.0 (code and weights) -- fully permissive. Clay v1.5: Apache-2.0 (code and weights) -- fully permissive. SatMAE: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (code and weights, per github.com/sustainlab-group/SatMAE/blob/main/LICENSE) -- NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY; acceptable for an academic capstone (a non-commercial research use) but this must be disclosed and would block any later commercial/deployed use of a SatMAE-derived model without a separate agreement. DINOv2: Apache-2.0 (code and weights) -- fully permissive. CLIP (OpenAI): MIT -- fully permissive. No licence in this set is unusable for the project as an academic exercise, but SatMAE's CC-BY-NC-4.0 is the one that must be flagged explicitly per the task's licence-verification requirement.
implementation.compute_requirement: CPU-only is genuinely sufficient for the intended use here, because only 42 forward passes (one per lake-year, or a few hundred if tiled to tokens) are needed through a FROZEN network -- no backpropagation through the large encoder at all. A single ViT-Large/600M forward pass on CPU takes on the order of seconds to a couple of minutes per patch; 42 of them is a coffee-break job on a laptop, not a training run. The practical bottleneck is disk/RAM for downloading and loading the larger checkpoints (Clay v1.5 ~5.16 GB, Prithvi-EO-2.0-600M ~2.4 GB) -- free Colab is useful mainly for its faster network/storage and optional GPU to speed this up, not because CPU inference is infeasible. Training only the small downstream linear/MLP head on 42 embeddings is trivial on CPU. The RS-MTDF-style distillation route is a different story: it requires an actual training loop (forward+backward) for the student network against two frozen teacher feature maps, which benefits materially from a free Colab/Kaggle T4 GPU, though the student itself is small enough to fit comfortably in free-tier GPU memory and finish in well under the session time limit.
implementation.student_days: Picking ONE encoder (Clay v1.5 or TerraMind v1.0 recommended on band-fit grounds, see below) and building a frozen-embedding + linear-probe pipeline: roughly 4-6 student-days (environment/weights setup 1, band alignment/resampling code 1-2, running inference and caching embeddings for 42 lake-years 0.5, building and cross-validating the linear head 1-2, writeup 0.5-1). Comparing multiple encoders (as the note requests) adds roughly 1-2 extra days per additional model, mostly band-adapter and licence-check overhead, so a full 5-model comparison realistically costs 10-15 student-days -- more than the project's 'one deep learning model' scope decision budgets for, so the honest recommendation is to prototype one (or at most two, contrasting a good-band-fit model against a poor one to make the comparison point) rather than all five. The RS-MTDF-style distillation alternative is NOT actually lighter to build: setting up two teacher forward passes, a feature-alignment loss, and a student training loop is more engineering than a linear probe on cached embeddings, an estimated 6-9 student-days; 'lighter' in the note refers to the deployed model's size, not the build effort.

evaluation.metrics: Because there is no real label, any classification/AUROC number against the MNDWI/NDVI-derived pseudo-labels only measures agreement with the existing baseline, not correctness -- it should be reported explicitly as a 'baseline-agreement' metric, not as accuracy against ground truth. More informative are: embedding-based clustering separation (silhouette score / cluster purity) between lake-years qualitatively known to differ (e.g. Bellandur's 2019 vs 2021 vs 2025 desilting episodes, which have an independently documented ha figure the student can sanity-check against), and a head-to-head comparison of the derived per-lake-year water/vegetation area estimate against the current classical baseline's numbers. Accuracy alone is inadequate given the near-total absence of confirmed positive (encroached) examples and the resulting severe class imbalance in any pseudo-labelled set.
evaluation.validation_protocol: Leave-one-lake-out (6 folds) for the downstream linear/MLP head, exactly as for every other item in this study -- pixels and patches within one lake's history are strongly spatially and spectrally correlated (same shoreline geometry, same sensor look-angle, same OSM polygon), so a naive random k-fold split on 42 rows drawn from only 6 underlying lakes leaks lake identity into the test fold. This is cheap to run here because the linear head is small and the frozen embeddings can be pre-computed once and reused across all 6 folds.
evaluation.leakage_risk: Two distinct risks beyond the usual spatial-autocorrelation-within-a-lake risk that also applies here: (1) pretraining-corpus contamination -- SSL4EO-S12 (251,079 global locations), Clay v1.5 (~70M global chips), TerraMind (9M TerraMesh samples), and Prithvi-EO-2.0 (4.2M global HLS time series) were all sampled globally and broadly from the same public Sentinel-2/Landsat archive the project itself draws from; it is plausible, though not confirmed, that tiles overlapping MGRS 43PGQ or the specific Bengaluru lakes were included in one or more of these pretraining sets. This is representation leakage (the encoder may already be 'familiar' with this exact geography), not label leakage, since none of these models ever saw an encroachment label -- but it should be disclosed as a caveat rather than presented as evidence the model 'understands' these lakes. (2) pseudo-label circularity -- evaluating the downstream head only against MNDWI/NDVI-derived pseudo-labels measures agreement with the seed rule, not a genuine improvement, exactly the same circularity risk noted for the from-scratch U-Net item.
evaluation.uncertainty_reporting: None of the five encoders provides a calibrated uncertainty by default; they output point embeddings. A defensible interval requires the student to bootstrap the downstream linear head (e.g. resample the 42 lake-year embeddings with replacement 1,000x and report a 90% interval on the derived risk score) or wrap the pipeline in conformal prediction, exactly as recommended elsewhere in this study for a 42-row, no-ground-truth setting. RS-MTDF-style distillation likewise yields only a point prediction from the trained student unless an ensemble of student seeds or Monte Carlo dropout is added.
evaluation.augmentation_honesty_risk: Not applicable to the frozen-encoder route itself (no synthetic time-series or tabular augmentation is involved in simply extracting embeddings). It becomes a real risk only if the student additionally oversamples or SMOTE-balances a rare 'encroached' pseudo-label class before training the linear head on only 42 rows -- this could manufacture an apparent class-separable trend that does not reflect natural prevalence, and must be disclosed explicitly if used, never presented as a natural finding.

evidence.published_performance: TerraMind v1.0 with a frozen encoder reaches an average mIoU of 66.58% on the PANGAEA multi-task benchmark, reported as best average rank among compared foundation models in the primary paper (Jakubik et al., ICCV 2025) [verify -- figure taken from a secondary summary of the paper's results table, not independently re-derived from the table itself in this session]. SatMAE's original paper reports pretraining gains of roughly 2-3 percentage points top-1 accuracy on EuroSAT and roughly 2 points mAP on BigEarthNet over from-scratch training with a ViT-Large backbone (Cong et al., NeurIPS 2022) [verify -- exact table values not independently re-derived]. SSL4EO-S12, Prithvi-EO-2.0, and Clay v1.5 all report downstream gains over from-scratch or ImageNet-initialised baselines on various benchmarks (BigEarthNet/EuroSAT for SSL4EO-S12; GEO-Bench across 0.1 m-15 m resolutions for Prithvi-EO-2.0; PhilEO Bench and various segmentation tasks for Clay), but no single, directly comparable headline number for all three was confirmed against a primary source in this session [verify]. RS-MTDF (Zhang et al. 2025, arXiv:2506.08772) reports state-of-the-art semi-supervised semantic segmentation results on ISPRS Potsdam, LoveDA, and DeepGlobe using frozen DINOv2+CLIP teachers, but all three benchmarks are sub-metre-to-few-metre RGB aerial/satellite imagery, not 20 m multispectral Sentinel-2, so the reported gains do not transfer directly to this project's resolution and band set.
evidence.study_area_of_that_work: TerraMind/PANGAEA: a multi-task global benchmark spanning several sensors and resolutions, not specifically 20 m 6-band urban wetland imagery. SatMAE/EuroSAT/BigEarthNet: European land-cover tiles, no urban lake, hyacinth, or desilting analogue. SSL4EO-S12/Clay/Prithvi downstream benchmarks: broad global land-cover and crop-type tasks, not lake water-body or wetland segmentation specifically. RS-MTDF: ISPRS Potsdam (German urban aerial imagery, ~5 cm GSD), LoveDA (Chinese urban/rural land cover, ~0.3-2 m aerial), DeepGlobe (sub-metre satellite land cover) -- none is a 20 m Sentinel-2, tropical, hyacinth-affected, seasonally-drained lake setting. No located result is a direct forecast for 6 Bengaluru lakes at this project's resolution.
evidence.applies_to_indian_urban_lakes: No. No published application of SSL4EO-S12, Prithvi-EO-2.0, TerraMind v1.0, Clay, SatMAE, or RS-MTDF-style distillation to Indian urban lakes or Bengaluru specifically was located during this research.
evidence.evidence_recency: SatMAE (2022, NeurIPS, arXiv:2207.08051) and SSL4EO-S12 (2022, arXiv:2211.07044) both predate the project's stated 2023-onward priority window for foundation models and should be treated as older, still-usable baselines rather than frontier evidence. Clay v1.5 (released September 2024), Prithvi-EO-2.0 (December 2024, arXiv:2412.02732), TerraMind v1.0 (April 2025, arXiv:2504.11171, ICCV 2025), and RS-MTDF (June 2025, arXiv:2506.08772) are all within the requested 2023-onward window and represent the current state of the art for frozen geo-foundation encoders.

risk.failure_modes: Band-contract mismatches are the dominant failure mode here and differ per model: SSL4EO-S12's main checkpoints expect the full 13-band L1C stack (or a 3-band RGB-only variant that discards B08/B11 entirely), neither of which matches the project's cached B02/B03/B04/B08/B11/SCL without re-downloading additional bands or accepting a degraded RGB-only representation. Prithvi-EO-2.0 expects Blue/Green/Red/NIR-narrow(B8A)/SWIR1(B11)/SWIR2(B12) at 30 m -- the project has B08 (wide NIR) not B8A, lacks B12 entirely, and is on the wrong grid (20 m vs 30 m); feeding B08 into the NIR-narrow slot silently uses the wrong spectral response curve, a subtle correctness bug, not a clean substitution. TerraMind v1.0 and Clay v1.5 explicitly support band subsetting/flexible band combinations, so are the most likely to accept the cached B02/B03/B04/B08/B11 set directly, but neither vendor documents accuracy degradation from dropping 5-7 of their nominal 10-12 bands, so quality with a reduced band set is unverified. SatMAE's grouped-band architecture (fixed index groups for 10 m/20 m/SWIR bands) is not designed to drop bands within a group, so the project's missing B05/B06/B07/B8A/B12 cannot simply be omitted without retraining the group-specific patch embeddings. RS-MTDF's DINOv2/CLIP teachers only accept 3-channel RGB and were never exposed to SWIR or NIR information at all, so B08 and B11 -- the two bands the project's own MNDWI/NDVI baseline actually depends on -- are invisible to this distillation route entirely, a serious and non-obvious limitation given the note's framing of it as a 'lighter alternative.'
risk.panel_defensibility: A panel will ask 'why does your foundation-model embedding do better than our simple MNDWI/NDVI rule, when you have no ground truth to check either against?' -- the honest answer is that without a labelled test set, any headline improvement number is unverifiable, and the only defensible claims are qualitative (does the embedding visibly separate hyacinth-mat years from open-water years better than the threshold rule, checked against the Bareuther 2020 macrophyte map for 2 of 6 lakes) or comparative-to-baseline (does the derived water-area track match or diverge from the classical number, and can the divergence be explained). A panel will also ask 'did you verify the model actually saw the bands it needed,' and for at least 3 of these 5 named models (SSL4EO-S12, Prithvi-EO-2.0, SatMAE) the honest answer given the current 6-band cache is 'not without re-downloading additional bands, and even then with an imperfect band-definition match for Prithvi.'
risk.honest_expectation: Realistically achievable: a modest, unverifiable-against-ground-truth improvement in feature quality for a downstream linear probe, most plausibly using TerraMind v1.0 or Clay v1.5 because they are the only two of the five that (a) explicitly support the project's exact cached band subset without retraining, (b) carry a fully permissive Apache-2.0 licence, and (c) were pretrained at a resolution reasonably close to 20 m. It will NOT manufacture ground truth, will NOT resolve the desilting confound, and will only speculatively help with the hyacinth confound pending a direct check against the Bareuther 2020 map. A null or 'no meaningful difference from the classical baseline' result on the headline encroachment question is a live and reportable possibility and should not be dressed up as a positive finding if the embeddings simply reproduce the MNDWI/NDVI pseudo-labels they were probed against.

verdict.recommended_rank: consider-with-reasons for TerraMind v1.0 or Clay v1.5 specifically (adopt-if-time only if the student has already committed to a different single deep-learning model for the guide's core deliverable and has spare days for a genuine ablation); reject for SSL4EO-S12, Prithvi-EO-2.0, and SatMAE as direct plug-ins to the current 6-band cache without additional band downloads and, for Prithvi, a resolution reconciliation; reject the RS-MTDF/DINOv2/CLIP distillation route as a primary method because its RGB-only teachers cannot see the NIR/SWIR bands the project's own baseline is built on, though it remains an interesting 'considered' comparison point for a lighter deployed model if band limitations are explicitly disclosed.
verdict.one_line_for_the_guide: We evaluated five pretrained Sentinel-2 foundation-model encoders as frozen feature extractors; only TerraMind v1.0 and Clay v1.5 cleanly accept our cached six bands and carry fully open licences, and even then the resulting features can only be checked qualitatively against our existing baseline, not against real encroachment ground truth, so we treat this as a supporting comparison rather than the project's primary deep-learning model.
